# neuron v0.1.3

Windows 10/11 (x86_64). The installer and portable ZIP include the tray app and CLI. The binaries are unsigned. Verify the download with `SHA256SUMS.txt`; `SOURCE.txt` names the source commit and build method, and the installer and ZIP carry GitHub build-provenance attestations.

Verified on Windows with a Naga V2 Pro, BlackWidow Chroma V2, and Overwatch as the Chroma game. Other platforms remain unverified.

Overwatch does a lot with Chroma. Every hero gets its own layout, abilities go dark and refill on their keys, an ult rolls a wave across the board. neuron already painted all of that onto my devices, but I couldn't see what the game was actually doing or do anything with it. v0.1.3 reads the game's lighting from the inside and takes it apart while you play. I also gave the whole interface one colour language, so a colour means the same thing on every page.

## Changed

- Added a Chroma lab under LIGHTING → VISITORS. It splits what a game paints into its ambient colour, the keys it holds, the keys it animates, and the effects it repeats. Effects keep their ids per game, so you name one once. Hover an effect to replay its last play on the board.
- Added scenes: the resting pictures a game keeps coming back to, like a menu or a hero. Flag one and neuron tells you when it ends while you're in another window, so you can tab out in the menu and still catch the match starting.
- An effect or scene can save a clip, switch an OBS scene or a profile, or mute your output. Game lighting can only trigger that kind of feedback; it can't press keys, click, or run anything.
- Hide an effect you don't want on your keys, restyle all game lighting with a hue, saturation and brightness lens, or carry the game's colours to any device with the new Game Light layer.
- Rewrote Chroma decoding against the real record layout of every device type. Mice, headsets, mousepads, keypads and room lights now decode correctly, Razer's built-in wave, spectrum, breathing and blink effects are drawn instead of misread as colours, and a paused game reads as paused. Lab captures also save as Razer `.chroma` animations.
- Every colour in the interface now answers one question: is it on, is it waiting for my input, is it settled, or can it not be undone. Each also has its own shape, so it still reads without colour. Faders gained click-to-type values, double-click to reset, and Shift for fine control, and scrolling past a maxed fader scrolls the page again.

The lab has been tuned on Overwatch. Other Chroma games should work, but I haven't tried them yet.
